source_text:
Φοβηθεὶς τοῦ
ὑμῖν ἀναγγεῖλαι τὴν ἐμαυτοῦ ἐπιστήμην. Ἐπαγγέλλεται μέντοι «ἐπιστήμην» ἔχειν,
ἢ, κατὰ τοὺς λοιποὺς, «γνῶσιν,» πῶς ἄν θρωποι πάσχουσιν ἐν τῷ βίῳ· πῶς τινες
ἄδικοι εὐτυχοῦσιν. Εἶδον ἀδικοῦντας καὶ παρανομοῦν τας, εὐθηνοῦντας, καὶ ἐμοῦ
παραμικρὸν ἐσα λεύθησαν οἱ πόδες, ἐὰν ἐν τῷ βίῳ τούτῳ μόνῳ ἐνίδω· ἐὰν δὲ τὸ
μέλλον ἐννοήσω, ἑστῶτές εἰσιν οἱ πόδες μου. ∆ιὸ εἶπα· Ἀκούσατέ μου. Ἕτερα
ἀντίγραφα μετὰ τὸ «Ἐρῶ γὰρ ὑμῶν ἀκουόντων,» ἔχει καὶ τού τους στίχους· «Ἰδοὺ
ἤκουσα τοὺς λόγους ὑμῶν, ἠνωτισάμην ἄχρι συνέσεως ὑμῶν.» Οἱ δὲ ἕτεροι ἑρ
μηνευταὶ οὕτως ἐκδεδώκασιν· «Ἰδοὺ, ἐξεδεξάμην τοὺς λόγους ὑμῶν· ἠκροασάμην
ἐφ' ὅσον ἐφρονεῖτε, ἐφ' ὅσον ἐξητάζετε λόγους, καὶ μέχρι τοῦ ἐφικέσθαι ὑμῶν,
ἐνενόουν.» Κατὰ μὲν οὖν ταύτην τὴν ἔκδοσιν καὶ τὰ ἕτερα τῶν ἀντιγράφων, Ὥσπερ,
φησὶν, ἐγὼ μεθ' ἡσυχίας ἤκουσα πάντων ὧν εἴπατε, καὶ ἀνέμεινα μέχρι
συμπεράσματος τῶν ὑμετέρων λόγων· καὶ ἕως ὅτε πᾶσαν ἑαυτῶν τὴν φρόνησιν
κενώσητε· καὶ ὑμεῖς τῶν ἐμῶν ἀκούσατε λόγων. Κατὰ δὲ τὰ παρ' ἡμῖν ἀντίγραφα ὁ
νοῦς οὗτος· Ἀκούσατέ μου, φησίν· ἐρῶ γὰρ οὐδὲν ὑπέρογκον, ἀλλ' ἃ δύνασθε
δοκιμάσαι. «Καὶ μέχρις ὑμῶν συνήσω,» ἀντὶ τοῦ, Οὐ κενοφω νίαις χρήσομαι, ἀλλ' ὡς
δύνασθε συνιέναι λαλήσω. Ἢ ἐκεῖνό φησιν, ὅτι, Οὐ πρότερον παύσομαι λαλῶν, πρὶν
ἢ καὶ ὑμεῖς τοὺς ἐμοὺς δοκιμάσητε λόγους, εἰ ἄρα κἀγὼ συνιέναι δύναμαι «μέχρις
ὑμῶν,» τουτ έστι, μέχρις οὗ καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐννοήσητε, ἢ καὶ ὑπερ βάλλω τὴν ὑμετέραν
σύνεσιν. Πλήρης γάρ εἰμι ῥημάτων. Καλῶς εἶπε τὸ, «πλή ρης εἰμί·» ὁ γὰρ μὴ πλήρης
ὢν ῥημάτων, καὶ ἐρ χόμενος ἐπὶ τὸ λαλεῖν, κενὰ λαλήσει ὡς κενὸς, κατὰ τὸ
εἰρημένον· «Ὁ γὰρ μωρὸς μωρὰ λαλήσει, καὶ ἡ καρδία αὐτοῦ μάταια νοήσει.» Ὀλέκει
γάρ με τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς γαστρός. Ὥσπερ τις ἔγκυος γίνεται, καὶ μορφωθέντος τοῦ
γεννωμέ νου ἐν αὐτῇ ἐπὶ ὠδῖνας ἔρχεται, μέχρις οὗ ἀπογεν 12.1044 νήσῃ τὸ
συλληφθέν· κατὰ ταῦτα δὲ καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς φιλομα θοῦς ψυχῆς γίνεται· συλλαμβάνει γὰρ
τὸν λόγον, ὃν ἀπαγγελλόμενον μορφοῖ, καὶ τυποῖ αὐτὸν τῇ τάξει· ὅταν δὲ μετὰ τὸ
τυπῶσαι καὶ μορφῶσαι, τετελειωμέ νον αὐτὸν παραδῷ, τότε τίκτει· καὶ μέχρις ἂν
τέκῃ, βαρύνεται ἐν ὠδῖνι. Λαλήσω, ἵνα ἀναπαύσωμαι ἀνοίξας τὰ χείλη. Ὁ τυγχάνων
συνετοῦ ἀκροατοῦ, καὶ ὢν πλήρης λό γων, λαλῶν ἀναπαύεται, τὴν περισσότητα
οἷον κενώ σας καὶ ἀποβαλών. ΚΕΦ. ΛΕʹ. Ἀνάβλεψον εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν. Ἀναβλέπει εἰς
τὸν οὐρανὸν οὐχ ὁ τοὺς σωματικοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἐπάρας, καὶ ἰδὼν τὸν οὐρανόν·
τοῦτο γὰρ τὸ ἀναβλέπειν ἔχουσι καὶ οἱ κύνες καὶ οἱ ὄνοι. Οὐδεὶς φιλόκοσμος ἀναβλέ
πει εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν, ἀλλ' ὁ μὴ ἀγαπῶν τὸν κόσμον, μηδὲ τὰ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ. Πάλιν δὲ
οὐχ οὕτω τὰ νέφη ὑψηλὰ ἀφ' ἡμῶν ἐστιν, ὡς ἐὰν ἴδω τὸν Μω σέως βίον, καὶ τὴν
ἐκείνου πρὸς Θεὸν ἀρέσκειαν, καὶ τὴν ἐμαυτοῦ σμικρότητα καὶ ταπεινότητα, οὕτω
βλέ πω τὸ νέφος ὑψηλὸν ἀπ' ἐμοῦ· ἐὰν ἔλθω ἐπὶ Ἰησοῦν τὸν τοῦ Ναυῆ, ἐπὶ τοὺς
βίους τῶν προφητῶν, ἐὰν ἐξ ετάζω αὐτῶν τὰς πράξεις, τότε ποιῶ τὸ γεγραμμέ νον,
καὶ καταμανθάνω πόσον ἐστὶ τὰ νέφη ὑψηλὰ ἀπ' ἐμοῦ. Εἰ ἥμαρτες, τί πράξεις; Ἆρα
οὖν, φησὶν, οἶδας, εἰ ἥμαρτες, τί πράξεις ἐπὶ τὸ λῦσαι τὸ ἡμαρτημένον; Εἰ ἥμαρτες
λόγοις, λόγοις κρείττοσιν ἴασαι· εἰ ἥμαρ τες ἐν ἔργοις, ἔργοις διαφέρουσιν αὐτὸς
ἑαυτὸν ἰώ μενος· εἰ δὲ πολλαὶ καὶ ἀνίατοι αἱ ἀνομίαι, διὰ τοῦτο ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀνιάτοις, οἷς
ἑαυτοὺς ἰάσασθαι οὐ δυνάμεθα, ἦλθεν Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ἐξ οὐρανῶν, ἵνα τὰ ἀνίατα ἰά
σηται, καὶ γένηται τὸ, «Μακάριοι ὧν ἀφέθησαν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι.» Ὁ κατατάσσων
φυλακὰς νυκτερινάς. Ὅρα ὅτι ἐγκώμια τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ὕμνους διεξέρχεται ὁ Ἐλιοῦς,
λέγων περὶ αὐτοῦ, «Ὁ κατατάσσων φυλακὰς νυκτε ρινάς.» Θέλεις ἰδεῖν πῶς
κατατάσσει φυλακὰς νυ κτερινὰς ὁ Θεός; Ὅλος ὁ αἰὼν οὗτος νύξ ἐστι, σκό τος ἐστί.
Τὸ φῶς τηρεῖταί σοι· νῦν γὰρ δι' ἐσόπτρου βλέπεις, μέλλεις δέ ποτε βλέπειν τὸ φῶς.
Οὐκοῦν νύξ ἐστι πᾶς ὁ αἰὼν, καὶ χρεία φυλάκων τεταγμένων εἰς νύκτα ταύτην, ἵνα
οἱ φύλακες, οἱ ἐπὶ τῶν νυκτῶν, φρου ρῶσι τοὺς ἐν νυξὶν ἀπὸ τῶν λῃστῶν, ἀπὸ τῶν
θηρίων, ἀπὸ τῶν πολεμίων. Τίνες οἱ φύλακες; Οἱ παρεμβάλ λοντες ἄγγελοι. Ὁ
διορίζων με ἀπὸ τετραπόδων γῆς. Κατὰ δὲ τοὺς λοιποὺς, «διδάσκων ἡμᾶς ὑπὲρ τὰ
κτήνη τῆς γῆς, καὶ σοφίζων ὑπὲρ τὰ κατὰ τὸν ἀέρα διιπτάμενα πετεινά·» μόνος γὰρ ὁ
ἄνθρωπος λόγῳ τετίμηται.
thought_title: Elihu's speech: knowledge, birth of words, and God's night watches
orientation: Origen is expounding Elihu's speech in Job 32-37, where Elihu claims to speak with knowledge and praises God's ordering of the night watches.
pass_a_gloss: Having feared to announce to you my own knowledge. He promises indeed to have knowledge, or, according to the others, understanding, how men suffer in life; how some unjust people prosper. I saw those doing wrong and breaking the law, flourishing, and my feet were almost shaken, if I look at this life alone; but if I consider the future, my feet are standing. Therefore I said: Hear me. Other copies after the phrase 'For I will speak while you listen' also have these lines: 'Behold, I heard your words, I gave ear as far as your understanding went.' But the other translators have rendered it thus: 'Behold, I received your words; I listened as far as you thought, as far as you examined words, and until reaching you, I understood.' According then to this rendering and the other copies, Just as, he says, I with quietness heard all the things you said, and I waited until the conclusion of your words; and until you empty all your own thinking; you also hear my words. But according to the copies among us the sense is this: Hear me, he says; for I will speak nothing excessive, but things which you are able to test. 'And as far as you I will understand,' instead of, I will not use empty sounds, but I will speak as you are able to understand. Or he says that, I will not stop speaking before you also test my words, whether then I also am able to understand 'as far as you,' that is, until you also understand, or I even surpass your understanding. For I am full of words. Well did he say, 'I am full'; for the one who is not full of words, and comes to speaking, will speak empty things as an empty person, according to what is said: 'For the fool will speak foolish things, and his heart will think vain things.' For the spirit of the belly destroys me. Just as a woman becomes pregnant, and when the child being born is formed in her she comes to birth pangs, until she gives birth to what was conceived; in the same way it also happens with the learning-loving soul; for it conceives the word, which it forms as it is announced, and it shapes it with order; but when after shaping and forming, it delivers it perfected, then it gives birth; and until it gives birth, it is weighed down in birth pang. I will speak, so that I may rest, having opened my lips. The one who has an intelligent hearer, and is full of words, rests when speaking, having as it were emptied and cast off the excess. Chapter 35. Look up to heaven. He looks up to heaven not the one who raises bodily eyes and sees heaven; for this looking up even dogs and donkeys have. No lover of the world looks up to heaven, but the one who does not love the world, nor the things in the world. Again the clouds are not so high from us, as when I see the life of Moses, and his pleasingness to God, and my own smallness and lowliness, so I see the cloud high from me; if I come to Joshua son of Nun, to the lives of the prophets, if I examine their deeds, then I do what is written, and I learn how much the clouds are high from me. If you sinned, what will you do? So then, he says, do you know, if you sinned, what you will do to undo what was sinned? If you sinned in words, heal with better words; if you sinned in deeds, heal yourself with superior deeds; but if the lawless acts are many and incurable, therefore for the incurable things, which we cannot heal ourselves, Jesus Christ came from heaven, so that he might heal the incurable things, and it might happen, 'Blessed are those whose sins were forgiven.' The one who orders night watches. See that Elihu goes through praises and hymns of God, saying about him, 'The one who orders night watches.' Do you want to see how God orders night watches? This whole age is night, it is darkness. The light is kept for you; for now you see through a mirror, but you are going at some time to see the light. Therefore the whole age is night, and there is need of guards appointed for this night, so that the guards, those on the nights, may guard those in nights from robbers, from wild beasts, from enemies. Who are the guards? The angels who encamp around. The one who separates me from the four-footed creatures of the earth. But according to the others, 'teaching us beyond the cattle of the earth, and making wise beyond the winged birds that fly through the air'; for man alone has been honored with reason.

choices.why: The glossary does not fix this term, but 'knowledge' preserves the distinction Elihu draws between his own claim (ἐπιστήμη) and the alternative rendering (γνῶσις, 'understanding').
The glossary mandates 'night watches' for this term, used of the angelic guards over the dark age.
The image is of a pregnant woman in labor; 'birth pangs' keeps the physical, painful sense of the metaphor for the soul bringing forth the word.
The compound φιλομαθής means 'loving to learn'; rendering it as 'learning-loving' preserves the compound structure without a hyphenated English compound.

choices.english: the one who orders night watches
choices.why: The participle κατατάσσων means 'arranging' or 'ordering'; 'orders' keeps the active divine action of appointing the watches.
rejected: the one who sets night watches

bible_refs.note: ὁ γὰρ μωρὸς μωρὰ λαλήσει, καὶ ἡ καρδία αὐτοῦ μάταια νοήσει
ὁ διορίζων με ἀπὸ τετραπόδων γῆς

pass_b_english: Elihu says: “I was afraid to announce my own knowledge to you.” He does claim to have knowledge—or, according to the other Greek translations, understanding—of how people suffer in this life, and how some who are unjust flourish. I have seen people committing injustice and breaking the law, and yet thriving, and my feet were nearly shaken—if I look at this life alone; but if I consider what is to come, my feet stand firm. That is why he says: “Listen to me.”

Some manuscripts, after “For I will speak while you listen,” also have these lines: “Behold, I have heard your words, and I gave ear as far as your understanding went.” The other Greek translators have rendered it this way: “Behold, I have received your words; I listened as long as you were thinking, as long as you were examining words, and I understood until I reached you.” According to that version and those manuscripts, Elihu means this: Just as I listened in silence to everything you said, and waited until you finished your speeches, and until you emptied out all your own thinking, so you also listen to my words. But according to the manuscripts we use, the sense is this: “Listen to me,” he says, “for I will say nothing excessive, but only what you can test. And I will understand as far as you do.” That means: I will not use empty sounds, but I will speak in a way you can follow. Or he means this: I will not stop speaking before you test my words, to see whether I too can understand as far as you do—that is, as far as you can grasp—or whether I even surpass your understanding.

“For I am full of words” (Job 32:18). He was right to say “I am full.” For someone who is not full of words, and yet comes to speak, will speak empty things because he is empty, according to what is written: “For the fool will speak foolish things, and his heart will think empty thoughts” (Isaiah 32:6).

“The spirit of my belly destroys me.” Just as a woman becomes pregnant, and when the child is formed within her she comes to birth pangs until she gives birth to what she has conceived, so it also happens with a soul that loves learning. It conceives the word, and as it is announced it shapes it and forms it with order. When it has shaped and formed it and hands it over complete, then it gives birth. And until it gives birth, it is weighed down in birth pangs. “I will speak, so that I may find rest, opening my lips.” The person who has an intelligent hearer, and is full of words, finds rest in speaking, since he empties out and casts off his overflow.

Chapter 35. “Look up to the sky” (Job 35:5). The person who looks up to the sky is not the one who raises his bodily eyes and sees the sky; dogs and donkeys have that kind of looking up. No lover of the world looks up to the sky, but only the one who does not love the world or the things in the world. Again, the clouds are not as high above us as this: if I look at the life of Moses, and his pleasing of God, and my own smallness and lowliness, that is how I see the cloud high above me. If I come to Joshua son of Nun, to the lives of the prophets, if I examine their deeds, then I do what is written, and I learn how high the clouds are above me.

“If you have sinned, what will you do?” Elihu says: “Do you know, if you have sinned, what you will do to undo the sin?” If you have sinned in words, heal yourself with better words. If you have sinned in deeds, heal yourself with deeds that excel. But if your transgressions are many and incurable, then for the incurable things that we cannot heal ourselves, Jesus Christ came from heaven, so that he might heal the incurable, and so that it might be fulfilled: “Blessed are those whose sins are forgiven” (Psalm 32:1).

“The one who orders night watches” (Job 35:10). See how Elihu goes through praises and hymns of God, saying about him, “The one who orders night watches.” Do you want to see how God orders night watches? This whole age is night; it is darkness. The light is kept for you. For now you see through a mirror (1 Corinthians 13:12), but one day you will see the light. So this whole age is night, and there is need of guards appointed for this night, so that the guards, those on duty through the nights, may protect those who are in the night from robbers, from wild beasts, from enemies. Who are the guards? The angels who encamp around.

“The one who separates me from the four-footed creatures of the earth” (Job 35:11). According to the other Greek translators: “The one who teaches us beyond the beasts of the earth, and makes us wise beyond the birds that fly through the air.” For the human being alone has been honored with reason.

problems.quote: The spirit within me destroys me
problems.source_quote: Ὀλέκει γάρ με τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς γαστρός
problems.why: 'γαστρός' means 'belly/womb,' not 'within me' generally. The image is of pregnancy/birth pangs that follows, so 'spirit of the womb/belly' or 'spirit of my womb' is meant.
problems.fix: For the spirit of my womb consumes me
problems.ruling: Greek πνεῦμα τῆς γαστρὸς = ‘spirit of the womb’; English ‘spirit within me’ loses specific metaphor.

problems.why: The brief states to use LXX Psalm numbering where it differs from Hebrew. 'Blessed are those whose sins are forgiven' is Psalm 32:1 in Hebrew but Psalm 31:1 in LXX numbering. Origen cites the Greek OT (LXX), so this should be Psalm 31:1.
problems.ruling: Greek cites LXX Psalm 31:1; English references Psalm 32:1 mis‑numbers the citation.

edits.old: The spirit within me destroys me
edits.new: The spirit of my womb consumes me

fixed: Changed 'The spirit within me destroys me' to 'The spirit of my womb consumes me' because the source 'Ὀλέκει γάρ με τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς γαστρός' refers to the womb/belly, matching the pregnancy imagery that follows.
Changed 'Psalm 32:1' to 'Psalm 31:1' because the brief specifies LXX Psalm numbering, and 'Blessed are those whose sins are forgiven' is Psalm 31:1 in the LXX.

problems.quote: Elihu was afraid to announce his own knowledge to you.
problems.source_quote: Φοβηθεὶς τοῦ ὑμῖν ἀναγγεῖλαι τὴν ἐμαυτοῦ ἐπιστήμην.
problems.why: English hides that this is Origen quoting Elihu's words, not Elihu speaking directly.
problems.fix: Elihu says: 'I was afraid to announce my own knowledge to you.'
problems.ruling: Greek says Origen, not Elihu, is afraid; English misattributes speaker.

problems.quote: I have seen people committing injustice
problems.why: English shifts to first person without marking Elihu as speaker; seems like Origen speaking.
problems.fix: Mark as Elihu's speech: 'I have seen,' he says, 'people committing injustice...'
problems.ruling: First‑person verb Εἶδον is Origen’s observation; English lacks attribution, misleading.

problems.quote: That is why I said, "Listen to me."
problems.why: First person without attribution; reader cannot tell this is Elihu quoted, not Origen.
problems.fix: He says, 'That is why I said, "Listen to me."'
problems.ruling: Διὸ εἶπα is Origen speaking; English presents as Elihu’s words, misattributing.

problems.quote: Elihu says: Just as I listened in silence
problems.source_quote: Ὥσπερ, φησὶν, ἐγὼ μεθ' ἡσυχίας ἤκουσα
problems.why: English inserts 'Elihu says' late; earlier first-person passages unattributed, confusing speaker shifts.
problems.fix: Attribute all first-person quotations to Elihu consistently.
problems.ruling: Early first‑person passages lack speaker tag; later “Elihu says” is too late, causing confusion.

problems.quote: Does he mean: Do you know, if you have sinned
problems.source_quote: Ἆρα οὖν, φησὶν, οἶδας, εἰ ἥμαρτες, τί πράξεις
problems.why: English 'Does he mean' obscures that φησὶν marks Elihu as speaker; 'he' is ambiguous.
problems.fix: Elihu says: 'Do you know, if you have sinned, what you will do...'
problems.ruling: Greek φησὶν marks Elihu; English “Does he mean” leaves ‘he’ ambiguous.

problems.quote: The spirit of my womb consumes me
problems.source_quote: Ὀλέκει γάρ με τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς γαστρός
problems.why: Ὀλέκει means 'destroys' or 'kills', not 'consumes'; 'consumes' is too weak.
problems.fix: The spirit of my womb destroys me

problems.quote: as it is delivered it shapes it
problems.why: ἀπαγγελλόμενον means 'being announced/declared', not 'delivered' (as in birth); confuses the metaphor.
problems.fix: as the word is declared, it shapes it

problems.quote: I will understand as far as you do
problems.why: συνήσω is future 'I will understand', but context suggests 'I will speak so that you understand' or 'I will be understood as far as you'. Actually ambiguous; could mean 'I will understand up to your level'.
problems.ruling: συνήσω likely means ‘I will be understood’, not ‘I will understand as far as you do’.

problems.why: Unattributed first person; should be marked as Elihu speaking.
problems.ruling: Unattributed first‑person Εἶδον misleads about speaker, similar to item 2.

problems.quote: “Blessed are those whose sins are forgiven” (Psalm 31:1).
problems.source_quote: «Μακάριοι ὧν ἀφέθησαν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι.» (the beatitude quoted in Job 35:10‑11)
problems.why: The beatitude is Psalm 32:1 in the LXX, not Psalm 31:1.
problems.ruling: LXX Psalm 31:1 is not the beatitude; LXX Ps 32:1 has «Μακάριοι ὧν ἀφέθησαν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι». Numbering differs from Hebrew.

fixed: Elihu was afraid to announce his own knowledge to you: source is Elihu's first-person speech quoted by Origen; added quotation and attribution.
I have seen people committing injustice: source is Elihu's first-person speech; added 'he says' and quotation marks.
That is why I said, 'Listen to me': source is Elihu's first-person speech; added 'He says' and quotation marks.
Does he mean: Do you know, if you have sinned: source has φησὶν marking Elihu as speaker; changed to 'Elihu says' with quotation.
The spirit of my womb consumes me: Ὀλέκει means 'destroys', not 'consumes'; changed to 'destroys'.
as it is delivered it shapes it: ἀπαγγελλόμενον means 'being announced', not 'delivered'; changed to 'as it is announced'.
Psalm 31:1: LXX numbering is Psalm 32:1; changed citation.

problems.quote: Blessed are those whose sins are forgiven” (Psalm 32:1)
problems.why: The words are LXX Psalm 31:1; Hebrew 32 is the wrong numbering for this work.
problems.fix: “Blessed are those whose sins are forgiven” (Psalm 31:1).
problems.ruling: Source Μακάριοι ὧν ἀφέθησαν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι is LXX Psalm 31:1; the work uses LXX numbering (Job, Isaiah 32:6), so 'Psalm 32:1' misdirects the reference.

problems.quote: The spirit within me destroys me.
problems.source_quote: Ὀλέκει γάρ με τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς γαστρός
problems.why: γαστρός is the belly, the image the pregnancy comparison depends on.
problems.fix: “The spirit of my belly destroys me.”
problems.ruling: τῆς γαστρός ('of the belly') is dropped in 'within me'. The pregnancy image that follows depends on the belly, so the translation loses the anchor.

edits.old: "Blessed are those whose sins are forgiven" (Psalm 32:1).
edits.new: "Blessed are those whose sins are forgiven" (Psalm 31:1).

edits.old: The spirit within me destroys me.
edits.new: The spirit of my belly destroys me.

fixed: Psalm citation corrected to LXX numbering: Psalm 31:1 per source 'Μακάριοι ὧν ἀφέθησαν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι'.

problems.quote: and I gave ear until I understood you
problems.why: ἄχρι συνέσεως ὑμῶν means he listened as far as their understanding went, not until he understood them.
problems.fix: Behold, I have heard your words, and I gave ear as far as your understanding went.
problems.ruling: ἄχρι συνέσεως ὑμῶν means 'until your understanding'. ὑμῶν is the hearers' understanding. 'Until I understood you' makes it his comprehension of them, which shifts the sense.

edits.old: Behold, I have heard your words, and I gave ear until I understood you.

fixed: Fixed translation of ἄχρι συνέσεως ὑμῶν: it means 'as far as your understanding [went/reached]', not 'until I understood you'. The English now matches the source and gloss.

problems.quote: He says: “I have seen people committing injustice and breaking the law, and yet thriving, and my feet were nearly shaken—if I look at this life alone; but if I consider what is to come, my feet stand firm.”
problems.source_quote: Εἶδον ἀδικοῦντας καὶ παρανομοῦντας, εὐθηνοῦντας, καὶ ἐμοῦ παραμικρὸν ἐσαλεύθησαν οἱ πόδες, ἐὰν ἐν τῷ βίῳ τούτῳ μόνῳ ἐνίδω· ἐὰν δὲ τὸ μέλλον ἐννοήσω, ἑστῶτές εἰσιν οἱ πόδες μου.
problems.why: This is Origen’s first-person psalm reflection, not a speech introduced as Elihu’s. Elihu resumes at “Therefore I said.”
problems.fix: I have seen people doing wrong and breaking the law, and thriving, and my feet were nearly shaken—if I look only at this life; but if I consider what is to come, my feet stand firm.
problems.ruling: Source has no "φησίν" before "Εἶδον ἀδικοῦντας... οἱ πόδες μου"; adding "He says:" and quotes misattributes the commentator's first-person psalm reflection to Elihu.

last_rejected.quote: and I understood until I reached you
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ μέχρι τοῦ ἐφικέσθαι ὑμῶν, ἐνενόουν
last_rejected.why: The genitive ὑμῶν is the subject of ἐφικέσθαι: until you attain something. ἐνενόουν is “I was pondering,” not “I understood.”
last_rejected.fix: and, until you reached that point, I was pondering.
last_rejected.ruling: In Greek, ἐφικέσθαι takes a genitive object (ὑμῶν, 'reach you'), not a genitive subject; ἐνενόουν ('ponder/understand') is within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: that is, as far as you can grasp
last_rejected.source_quote: τουτέστι, μέχρις οὗ καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐννοήσητε
last_rejected.why: The gloss is temporal: until you too come to understand, not a limit of what you can grasp.
last_rejected.fix: that is, until you too come to understand
last_rejected.ruling: μέχρις οὗ glosses μέχρις ὑμῶν as a degree, contrasted with ὑπερβάλλω τὴν ὑμετέραν σύνεσιν; 'as far as you can grasp' is accurate, not temporal.

last_rejected.why: Those words are LXX Psalm 31:1. English Psalm 32:1 is the Hebrew number.
last_rejected.ruling: Psalm 32:1 is the standard English numbering for LXX Psalm 31:1 (Μακάριοι ὧν ἀφέθησαν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι), a convention preference rather than a wrong reference.
